title: Register machines need eight instructions to show complex behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Register machines need eight instructions to show complex behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among two-register machines with increment and decrement-jump instructions, all programs of up to four instructions behave repetitively, only two five-instruction programs give nesting, none up to seven instructions is substantially more complicated, and 126 of the 11,019,960,576 eight-instruction programs show complex behavior.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But with eight instructions, 126 out of the 11,019,960,576 possible programs finally do show more complicated behavior.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “Register Machines” (from p. 97), p. 99. Scope: two-register machines with increment and decrement-jump instructions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The counts are in principle exactly reproducible and lower instruction counts are easy to check. A fresh exhaustive eight-instruction validation is computationally substantial and classification of nonhalting long transients may require specialized methods, so full present resolution is limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reproduce the instruction encoding, exhaustively enumerate programs through seven instructions, and use symmetry reduction and parallel execution for all eight-instruction programs. Classify trajectories with fixed repetition, nesting, and complexity criteria and compare exact counts with 2 and 126.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ultimate behavior and long transients are difficult to certify.

Eleven billion eight-instruction programs exceed a small team's weeks-scale standard analysis.

Substantially more complicated requires a threshold.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Every integer in the claim is a count over an explicitly defined finite set of two-register programs. An optimized interpreter classifies the short lengths quickly and the length-eight set, about 1.1 times 10 to the 10 programs, within the reach of a small team in weeks because almost all programs are rejected by a short cycle check. The soft phrase 'substantially more complicated' at length seven is the main source of classifier risk; the length-eight count is then a direct comparison with 126.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate two-register increment and decrement-jump programs by length, up to eight instructions, and classify each as repetitive, nested, or complex under a fixed detector. The claim is confirmed if the short lengths match the stated census (all programs through four instructions repetitive, two nested programs at length five, none substantially more complex through seven, and 126 complex programs among 11,019,960,576 of length eight) and refuted if those integers change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Length-eight exhaustive search is large, though most programs die or cycle in a few dozen steps.

The count of 126 moves if the boundary between nested and complex programs moves.
